result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) is invoked synchronously in perform_retrieve, and poll_feed iterates the entire feed (rss.items.each) doing imports for every item, with no per-item dedup short-circuit besides content_sha1 in TopicEmbed.import. A concurrent cache miss (retrieved_recently? throttles per embed_url, not the feed) will re-fetch and re-import the whole feed. This is a real, specific performance/scalability concern in newly added code, not an outright correctness defect, so it fits important_non_bug.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real architectural concern in the diff. Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 33-46, the `perform_retrieve` method checks if a TopicEmbed exists, then calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` which processes ALL feed items (see app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb lines 27-35 iterating through `rss.items.each`). The throttle in `retrieved_recently?` (lines 22-31) uses Redis setnx with 60-second expiry, but this only prevents the same URL from being retrieved twice within 60 seconds. If multiple different URLs have cache misses concurrently, each will trigger a full feed poll. This is a legitimate scalability/efficiency concern about the design, though not a correctness bug - the code will work, just inefficiently under concurrent load.
